layout.notes: One block; floor section headings (e.g. 'GROUND FLOOR - RETAIL', '1ST FLOOR') and blank separator rows are excluded. Header on row 4, first section heading on row 5, so first unit is row 6. Last unit row is 199; row 200 is blank, row 201 is the TOTAL row (B201 is text '170 units'), row 203 is a footnote. Vacant rows have tenant text 'VACANT' and empty dates, rent, cheques, deposit and Ejari; no asking rent is shown. Area is in sq ft. Rent is annual (AED). Dates are text like 01-Jul-25 (DD-Mon-YY). Column I is the number of cheques. Column A S.No is a running number. Ground floor G01/G02 are retail shops. Tenant type is not a column (many tenants are companies, e.g. L.L.C.). Status column exists with mixed case variants.

discrepancies.title: OM income AED 14,270,000 vs in-place rent AED 12,675,000

sources.label: rent roll in-place rent, 153 let units
in-place rent plus screen reference rent on the vacant units (the roll shows no asking rents)

discrepancies.why: The OM figure is not contracted income: it is close to in-place rent plus screen reference rent on the vacant units (AED 14,232,450). The screen underwrites let units at their contract rent and vacant units at the screen reference rent after downtime. Gross yield on price falls from 7.4% to 6.5% on in-place rent.

impact.basis: OM stated income above rent-roll in-place rent

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for signed leases or Ejari certificates behind any unit the OM counts as income; treat the rest as vacant.

discrepancies.title: 44.5% of in-place rent is from units let more than 10.0% above the screen reference

sources.label: 60 let units more than 10.0% above the screen reference rent
screen reference rent (a proxy, not the RERA index)

discrepancies.why: In a falling 2026 market these leases are expected to reset towards the screen reference at renewal or expiry, which takes about AED 781,504 a year off income as they roll; the engine models each reset at its expiry date. The mandate limit is 20.0% of income. The reference is a proxy: confirm the rents with the DLD Smart Rental Index calculator.

impact.basis: rent above the screen reference on over-rented leases, lost as each renews or expires

discrepancies.analyst_action: Check the over-rented leases' expiry dates and tenants; price the resets into the offer.

discrepancies.title: OM occupancy 97.0% vs rent roll 90.0%

sources.label: rent roll: 153 of 170 units let at 2026-11-15

discrepancies.why: The rent roll is unit-level and dated 2026-11-15; the OM figure (undated) is a headline the screen cannot trace to units. A gap of 7.0 points is about 12 units. This is the same gap as the OM's income figure (potential rent as income), where its impact is counted.

impact.basis: 12 units x average in-place rent AED 82,843: income the OM implies but the roll does not show (estimate)

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for the Ejari export and the vacancy list at the rent-roll date; reconcile the OM figure to unit numbers.

discrepancies.title: OM yield 7.4% is on asking price, before 6.2% acquisition costs

sources.label: acquisition costs (DLD 4%, broker, trustee, mortgage registration)

discrepancies.why: A buyer pays AED 12,007,791 on top of the price. On price plus costs the same income gives 6.9%.

impact.basis: OM income on price plus acquisition costs, minus the stated yield

discrepancies.analyst_action: Compare deals on yield on total cost; ask the broker to restate the yield on that basis.

discrepancies.title: OM calls the building "fully tenanted" on the cover but states 97% occupied inside
discrepancies.why: The OM contradicts itself. The cover says fully tenanted and page 2 says 97% occupied. The rent roll as of 15 Nov 2026 shows 90% let by units, with 17 vacant units, so neither OM figure holds. The headline income and the 7.36% ROI rest on this occupancy claim. The rule-based occupancy mismatch already covers 97% against 90%. This finding adds the cover's "fully tenanted" claim.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask the broker to withdraw or justify the "fully tenanted" claim. Get a dated, unit-level occupancy and Ejari schedule that reconciles to the rent roll, and reprice on in-place rent.

notices.text: Tenants' security deposits of AED 629,375 transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
Cheque profile: 36% of rent on 1-2 cheques, 49% of rent on 3-4 cheques, 15% of rent on 6 or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
Retail leases: permitted use, trade licences and VAT treatment of shop rents.

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Needs work**: Sorrel Heights misses the mandate on yield, return targets and over-renting, and the price that would meet the return target is far below asking.

Buy at AED 105.8m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], exit at 6.8% [[uw.exit_yield]]. That is 45% below asking [[uw.walk_away_vs_asking]], against the asking price of AED 194.0m [[deal.asking_price_aed]]. The assumption that most moves the walk-away price is the exit yield (50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] either way), which shifts it by AED 11.7m [[uw.walk_away_largest_swing_aed]]. The walk-away price and returns rest on the firm's house view (reference rent path, exit yield, vacancy and downtime), not on market evidence for this building.

## The deal
- Sorrel Heights, JVC: 170 units [[om.unit_count]], completed 2024 [[deal.completion_year]], freehold single title.
- Asking AED 194.0m [[deal.asking_price_aed]], or AED 1,468 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on net area. The OM's AED 1,028 per sq ft [[om.price_psf_stated]] is on built-up area.
- Direct leases, no master tenant. In-place rent is AED 12.7m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]], with 90% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] of units let and 17 [[rr.vacant_units]] vacant at the rent roll date of 15 November 2026 [[rr.as_of]]. Tenants pay chiller. The largest expiry window runs from 15 May 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] to 14 August 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]]: AED 3.5m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]] of rent, 28% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of the total.

## Returns
Unlevered, pre-tax:

| Metric | Result | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Unlevered IRR | a loss of 0.5% [[uw.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]] a year | at least 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] |
| Equity multiple | 0.98x [[uw.unlevered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | at least 1.30x [[mandate.target_unlevered_equity_multiple.threshold]] |
| Entry yield on price | 5.3% [[uw.entry_yield_on_price]] | none |
| Exit yield | 6.8% [[uw.exit_yield]] | none |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 5.0% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | at least 6.0% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] |

Year-1 NOI is AED 10.2m [[uw.noi_year1]]. Levered, the IRR is a loss of 4.2% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] a year and the multiple 0.81x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]]. Year-1 DSCR is 1.40x [[uw.dscr_year1]].

The OM's headline yield is 7.4% [[om.yield_stated]], on asking price with the income basis unstated. On a buyer's basis (Year-1 NOI on price plus acquisition costs) it is 5.0% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. That is a negative gap against the OM of 2.4 points [[uw.om_yield.gap_vs_stated]].

## What would make it fail
- **Price and exit.** Even with market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter, unlevered IRR is only 2.1% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]], against the 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] target. No grid case comes close.
- **Over-renting.** 44% [[uw.over_rent_share_of_income]] of in-place rent is from units let well above the screen reference, against a 20% [[mandate.max_over_rent_share_of_income.threshold]] limit. Resets take about AED 782k [[uw.over_rent_excess_at_expiry_aed]] a year off income as leases roll, in a market the house view has falling.
- **Expiry bunching.** 28% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of rent expires in one three-month window, the one described above. It passes the 40% [[mandate.max_lease_expiry_share_in_any_quarter.threshold]] limit, but it coincides with the reset risk.
- **Overstated income.** The OM's income and occupancy are not supported by the rent roll (below).

## Discrepancies
1. **OM income and occupancy (high).** The OM states rent of AED 14.3m [[om.annual_rent_stated]] and 97% [[om.occupancy_stated]] occupancy; its cover also says "fully tenanted". The rent roll shows AED 12.7m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] and 90% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]]. The OM income looks like in-place rent plus reference rent on vacant units, so it is not contracted income. The screen used the rent roll. Gross yield on in-place rent is 6.5% [[uw.gross_yield_in_place_on_price]], not 7.4% [[om.yield_stated]]. Impact: income overstated by AED 1.6m [[disc.potential_rent_as_income.impact_aed]]. The occupancy and "fully tenanted" claims are the same gap and are counted once here.
2. **Over-rented leases (high).** These are the leases above the screen reference (see failure points). Impact: AED 782k [[disc.over_rented_vs_market.impact_aed]] a year, lost as they renew or expire. The reference is a proxy, so confirm it externally.
3. **Yield before acquisition costs (medium).** The OM's 7.4% [[om.yield_stated]] ignores acquisition costs of 6.2% [[uw.acquisition_costs_pct_of_price]] of price. On price plus costs, the OM's own income gives 6.9% [[uw.om_yield.stated_income_on_total_cost]], 0.4 points [[disc.yield_excludes_acquisition_costs.impact_ratio]] lower.

Lower-severity items are not discussed.

## Checks before diligence
- Get signed leases or Ejari certificates behind every unit the OM counts as income; treat the rest as vacant.
- Get a dated, unit-level occupancy schedule. Ask the broker to withdraw or justify "fully tenanted" and to restate yield on total cost.
- Check expiry dates and tenants on the over-rented leases and price the resets into the offer. Confirm rents with the DLD Smart Rental Index calculator.
- Security deposits of AED 629k [[rr.deposits_aed]] transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
- Cheque profile: about 15% [[notice.cheque_profile]] of rent is on six or more cheques, which means more collection risk.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search, including buyer eligibility.
- Dubai Municipality completion certificate.
- Affection plan and permitted use.
- Ejari export reconciled unit by unit.
- Civil Defence certificates and cladding compliance.
- Retail leases: permitted use, trade licences, VAT.

## Assumptions
Exit yield is the higher of area yield and entry yield, plus 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] expansion and an age premium. Market rent falls 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1 and 1.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2, then rises 2.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]] in Years 3 to 5. Structural vacancy is 5.0% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] and collection loss 1.0% [[assume.collection_loss]]. Debt is sized at 1.40x [[assume.sizing_dscr]] cover, with a 45% [[assume.max_ltv]] LTV cap and 15-year [[assume.amortisation_years]] amortisation. That gives a loan of AED 67.5m [[uw.loan_aed]] at 35% [[uw.ltv]] LTV and 6.8% [[uw.interest_rate]] interest. The hold is 5 years [[uw.hold_years]]. No operating cost categories were filled from mandate defaults.
